sanskrit: śrutvā hanumato vākyaṃ yathāvad abhibhāṣitam rāmaḥ prītisamāyukto vākyam uttaram abravīt
english: Having heard Hanūmān's words spoken exactly as they were, Rāma, filled with joy, replied with the following words.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ hanumatā kāryaṃ sumahad bhuvi duṣkaram manasāpi yad anyena na śakyaṃ dharaṇītale
english: Hanūmān has accomplished an exceedingly great and difficult deed on earth — one that no other being on this earth could even conceive of in mind.

sanskrit: na hi taṃ paripaśyāmi yas tareta mahārṇavam anyatra garuṇād vāyor anyatra ca hanūmataḥ
english: I see no one who could cross the great ocean, save Garuḍa, or the Wind, or Hanūmān.

sanskrit: devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām apradhṛṣyāṃ purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇena surakṣitām
english: The city of Laṅkā, which is impregnable to gods, dānavas, yakṣas, gandharvas, nāgas, and rākṣasas, and which is well-guarded by Rāvaṇa —

sanskrit: praviṣṭaḥ sattvam āśritya jīvan ko nāma niṣkramet ko viśet sudurādharṣāṃ rākṣasaiś ca surakṣitām yo vīryabalasaṃpanno na samaḥ syād dhanūmataḥ
english: — who, having entered it by courage, could emerge alive? Who could enter that city so very hard to assault, guarded by rākṣasas, if he were not equal to Hanūmān in valor and might?

sanskrit: bhṛtyakāryaṃ hanumatā sugrīvasya kṛtaṃ mahat evaṃ vidhāya svabalaṃ sadṛśaṃ vikramasya ca
english: Hanūmān has performed a great service for his master Sugrīva, deploying his own strength in a manner befitting his valor.

sanskrit: yo hi bhṛtyo niyuktaḥ san bhartrā karmaṇi duṣkare kuryāt tadanurāgeṇa tam āhuḥ puruṣottamam
english: A servant who, when assigned by his master to a difficult task, accomplishes it with devotion — such a one is called a foremost among men.

sanskrit: niyukto nṛpateḥ kāryaṃ na kuryād yaḥ samāhitaḥ bhṛtyo yuktaḥ samarthaś ca tam āhuḥ puruṣādhamam
english: A servant who, though capable, qualified, and charged with the king's task, yet does not perform it — such a one is called the lowest of men.

sanskrit: tanniyoge niyuktena kṛtaṃ kṛtyaṃ hanūmatā na cātmā laghutāṃ nītaḥ sugrīvaś cāpi toṣitaḥ
english: Hanūmān, appointed to that charge, has fulfilled his duty; he has not made himself small, and Sugrīva too is gratified.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca raghuvaṃśaś ca lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābalaḥ vaidehyā darśanenādya dharmataḥ parirakṣitāḥ
english: I, scion of the Raghu lineage, and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa have today been saved — rightfully so — by the sight of Vaidehī.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu mama dīnasyā mano bhūyaḥ prakarṣati yad ihāsya priyākhyātur na kurmi sadṛśaṃ priyam
english: Yet this thought afflicts my wretched heart anew: that here I can render no fitting gift to him who has brought such glad tidings.

sanskrit: eṣa sarvasvabhūtas tu pariṣvaṅgo hanūmataḥ mayā kālam imaṃ prāpya dattas tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: This embrace of Hanūmān is my all — given by me to that great soul, availing myself of this moment as the only gift I have.

sanskrit: sarvathā sukṛtaṃ tāvat sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam sāgaraṃ tu samāsādya punar naṣṭaṃ mano mama
english: The search for Sītā has been accomplished — that much is well done. Yet now that we have come to the ocean, my heart is lost once more.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nāma samudrasya duṣpārasya mahāmbhasaḥ harayo dakṣiṇaṃ pāraṃ gamiṣyanti samāhitāḥ
english: How shall the monkeys reach the southern shore of this vast, hard-to-cross sea? That is the question that weighs upon my mind.

sanskrit: yady apy eṣa tu vṛttānto vaidehyā gadito mama samudrapāragamane harīṇāṃ kim ivottaram
english: Even though Vaidehī's news has been reported to me, what still remains unsolved is the matter of the monkeys crossing the ocean.

sanskrit: ity uktvā śokasaṃbhrānto rāmaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ hanūmantaṃ mahābāhus tato dhyānam upāgamat
english: Having spoken thus, Rāma the destroyer of foes, agitated by grief, the long-armed hero, fell into deep contemplation, Hanūmān beside him.

sanskrit: taṃ tu śokaparidyūnaṃ rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam uvāca vacanaṃ śrīmān sugrīvaḥ śokanāśanam
english: Then glorious Sugrīva spoke words that dispel grief to Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who was scorched by sorrow.

sanskrit: kiṃ tvaṃ saṃtapyase vīra yathānyaḥ prākṛtas tathā maivaṃ bhūs tyaja saṃtāpaṃ kṛtaghna iva sauhṛdam
english: Why do you afflict yourself, O hero, like any ordinary man? Do not be so; abandon your anguish as an ingrate abandons friendship.

sanskrit: saṃtāpasya ca te sthānaṃ na hi paśyāmi rāghava pravṛttāv upalabdhāyāṃ jñāte ca nilaye ripoḥ
english: I see no occasion for your anguish, O Rāghava, now that news of her has been received and the enemy's abode has been discovered.

sanskrit: dhṛtimāñ śāstravit prājñaḥ paṇḍitaś cāsi rāghava tyajemāṃ pāpikāṃ buddhiṃ kṛtvātmevārthadūṣaṇīm
english: You are steadfast, versed in the scriptures, wise, and learned, O Rāghava. Abandon this wicked thought that, like a foe to oneself, corrupts your purpose.

sanskrit: samudraṃ laṅghayitvā tu mahānakrasamākulam laṅkām ārohayiṣyāmo haniṣyāmaś ca te ripum
english: We shall cross the ocean, which teems with great crocodiles, scale Laṅkā, and slay your enemy.

sanskrit: nirutsāhasya dīnasya śokaparyākulātmanaḥ sarvārthā vyavasīdanti vyasanaṃ cādhigacchati
english: For the man who has lost his energy, who is despondent, whose soul is overwhelmed by grief — all his purposes founder, and calamity overtakes him.

sanskrit: ime śūrāḥ samarthāś ca sarve no hariyūthapāḥ tvatpriyārthaṃ kṛtotsāhāḥ praveṣṭum api pāvakam
english: All our monkey chieftains are brave and capable; for your sake they have roused their courage even to the point of entering fire itself.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ harṣeṇa jānāmi tarkaś cāsmin dṛḍho mama vikrameṇa samāneṣye sītāṃ hatvā yathā ripum
english: By their exuberance I know it, and my conviction in this is firm: I shall bring Sītā back by valor, having slain the enemy.

sanskrit: setur atra yathā vadhyed yathā paśyema tāṃ purīm tasya rākṣasarājasya tathā tvaṃ kuru rāghava
english: As to how a bridge may be built here, and how we may behold that city of the king of rākṣasas — give your command to that effect, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tāṃ hi purīṃ laṅkāṃ trikūṭaśikhare sthitām hataṃ ca rāvaṇaṃ yuddhe darśanād upadhāraya
english: Having seen that city of Laṅkā seated on the peak of Trikūṭa, consider Rāvaṇa already slain in battle — take that as certain from the very sight.

sanskrit: setubaddhaḥ samudre ca yāval laṅkā samīpataḥ sarvaṃ tīrṇaṃ ca vai sainyaṃ jitam ity upadhāryatām
english: Once a bridge is built across the sea and Laṅkā is close at hand, and once the whole army has crossed — consider it conquered.

sanskrit: ime hi samare śūrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ tad alaṃ viklavā buddhī rājan sarvārthanāśanī
english: These monkeys who can assume any form are heroes in battle. Enough then of this faint-hearted thinking, O king, that destroys all purposes.

sanskrit: puruṣasya hi loke 'smiñ śokaḥ śauryāpakarṣaṇaḥ yat tu kāryaṃ manuṣyeṇa śauṇḍīryam avalambatā śūrāṇāṃ hi manuṣyāṇāṃ tvadvidhānāṃ mahātmanām
english: In this world grief diminishes a man's heroism. What a man must do is hold fast to courage — especially men who are heroes and great souls like yourself.

sanskrit: vinaṣṭe vā pranaṣṭe vā śokaḥ sarvārthanāśanaḥ tvaṃ tu buddhimatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvaśāstrārthakovidaḥ
english: Whether in ruin or in loss, grief destroys all aims. But you are the foremost among the wise, thoroughly versed in the meaning of all the scriptures.

sanskrit: madvidhaiḥ sacivaiḥ sārtham ariṃ jetum ihārhasi na hi paśyāmy ahaṃ kaṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu rāghava
english: You ought to conquer the enemy here, together with ministers like me. I see no one in all three worlds, O Rāghava —

sanskrit: gṛhītadhanuṣo yas te tiṣṭhed abhimukho raṇe vānareṣu samāsaktaṃ na te kāryaṃ vipatsyate
english: — who could stand before you in battle once you have taken up your bow. With the monkeys engaged, your purpose shall not fail.

sanskrit: acirād drakṣyase sītāṃ tīrtvā sāgaram akṣayam tad alaṃ śokam ālambya krodham ālamba bhūpate
english: You shall see Sītā soon, once you have crossed the boundless sea. Enough of clinging to grief — take hold of wrath instead, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭāḥ kṣatriyā mandāḥ sarve caṇḍasya bibhyati laṅganārthaṃ ca ghorasya samudrasya nadīpateḥ
english: Sluggish kṣatriyas who take no action — all of them tremble before the fierce. And as for crossing the dreadful lord of rivers, the ocean —

sanskrit: sahāsmābhir ihopetaḥ sūkṣmabuddhir vicāraya ime hi samare śūrā harayaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: — having come here with us, consider the matter with your keen intellect. For these monkeys who can take any form are heroes in battle.

sanskrit: tān arīn vidhamiṣyanti śilāpādapavṛṣṭibhiḥ kathaṃ cit paripaśyāmas te vayaṃ varuṇālayam
english: They will scatter those enemies with showers of rocks and trees. Somehow we do see our way across the abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: kim uktvā bahudhā cāpi sarvathā vijayī bhavān
english: What more need be said at length? You shall be victorious in every way.

sanskrit: sugrīvasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetumat paramārthavit pratijagrāha kākutstho hanūmantam athābravīt
english: Having heard Sugrīva's well-reasoned speech, Kākutstha, knower of the highest truth, accepted it and then spoke to Hanūmān.

sanskrit: tarasā setubandhena sāgarocchoṣaṇena vā sarvathā susamartho 'smi sāgarasyāsya laṅghane
english: Whether by the swift building of a bridge or by drying up the ocean, I am fully capable in every way of crossing this sea.

sanskrit: kati durgāṇi durgāyā laṅkāyās tad bravīhi me jñātum icchāmi tat sarvaṃ darśanād iva vānara
english: How many fortifications does the fortified city of Laṅkā have? Tell me that. I wish to know all of it as if seeing it with my own eyes, O monkey.

sanskrit: balasya parimāṇaṃ ca dvāradurgakriyām api gupti karma ca laṅkāyā rakṣasāṃ sadanāni ca
english: The size of the army, the construction of the gates and fortifications, the defensive measures of Laṅkā, and the dwellings of the rākṣasas —

sanskrit: yathāsukhaṃ yathāvac ca laṅkāyām asi dṛṣṭavān saram ācakṣva tattvena sarvathā kuśalo hy asi
english: — all that you saw freely and exactly in Laṅkā, recount to me truly. For you are in every way an expert.

sanskrit: śrutvā rāmasya vacanaṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ vākyaṃ vākyavidāṃ śreṣṭho rāmaṃ punar athābravīt
english: Having heard Rāma's words, Hanūmān, son of the Wind, foremost among those skilled in speech, again spoke to Rāma.

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ sarvam ākhyāsye durgakarmavidhānataḥ guptā purī yathā laṅkā rakṣitā ca yathā balaiḥ
english: "Let me be heard; I shall relate everything, regarding the arrangement of the fortifications, how the city of Laṅkā is protected and how it is guarded by armed forces."

sanskrit: parāṃ samṛddhiṃ laṅkāyāḥ sāgarasya ca bhīmatām vibhāgaṃ ca balaughasya nirdeśaṃ vāhanasya ca
english: "The surpassing wealth of Laṅkā, the dreadfulness of the ocean, the arrangement of the army's divisions, and the disposition of the war-vehicles —"

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭā muditā laṅkā mattadvipasamākulā mahatī rathasaṃpūrṇā rakṣogaṇasamākulā
english: "Laṅkā is jubilant and cheerful, crowded with rutting elephants, large, filled with chariots, and thronged with bands of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: dṛḍhabaddhakavāṭāni mahāparighavanti ca dvārāṇi vipulāny asyāś catvāri sumahānti ca
english: "Her four vast gates are of great size, fitted with strongly fastened panels and great iron crossbars."

sanskrit: vapreṣūpalayantrāṇi balavanti mahānti ca āgataṃ parasainyaṃ tais tatra pratinivāryate
english: "On the ramparts stand great and powerful stone-throwing machines, by which any enemy force that arrives there is driven back."

sanskrit: dvāreṣu saṃskṛtā bhīmāḥ kālāyasamayāḥ śitāḥ śataśo rocitā vīraiḥ śataghnyo rakṣasāṃ gaṇaiḥ
english: "At the gates, dreadful śataghnis — heavy iron-bolt engines — forged of black iron, sharp and burnished, are ranged by the hundreds, mounted by warrior bands of rākṣasas."

sanskrit: sauvarṇaś ca mahāṃs tasyāḥ prākāro duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ maṇividrumavaidūryamuktāvicaritāntaraḥ
english: "She has a great golden rampart, hard to assail, whose interstices are inlaid with gems, coral, vaidūrya, and pearls."

sanskrit: sarvataś ca mahābhīmāḥ śītatoyā mahāśubhāḥ agādhā grāhavatyaś ca parikhā mīnasevitāḥ
english: "All around are great and terrifying moats, auspicious and vast, filled with cool water, fathomless, and inhabited by crocodiles and fish."

sanskrit: dvāreṣu tāsāṃ catvāraḥ saṃkramāḥ paramāyatāḥ yantrair upetā bahubhir mahadbhir dṛḍhasaṃdhibhiḥ
english: "Over those moats are four very long drawbridges fitted with many great and tightly jointed mechanisms."

sanskrit: trāyante saṃkramās tatra parasainyāgame sati yantrais tair avakīryante parikhāsu samantataḥ
english: "Those drawbridges are raised for defense when an enemy army approaches, and by those mechanisms they are dropped all around into the moats."

sanskrit: ekas tv akampyo balavān saṃkramaḥ sumahādṛḍhaḥ kāñcanair bahubhiḥ stambhair vedikābhiś ca śobhitaḥ
english: "But one bridge is immovable and strong, exceedingly firm and massive, adorned with many golden pillars and parapets."

sanskrit: svayaṃ prakṛtisaṃpanno yuyutsū rāma rāvaṇaḥ utthitaś cāpramattaś ca balānām anudarśane
english: "Rāvaṇa himself, O Rāma, is gifted by nature with martial spirit — ever roused and vigilant in the inspection of his forces."

sanskrit: laṅkā purī nirālambā devadurgā bhayāvahā nādeyaṃ pārvataṃ vanyaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ca caturvidham
english: "The city of Laṅkā is self-sustaining, a fortress of the gods, fearsome; she has all four kinds of natural fortification: riverine, mountainous, forest-based, and artificial."

sanskrit: sthitā pāre samudrasya dūrapārasya rāghava naupathaś cāpi nāsty atra nirādeśaś ca sarvataḥ
english: "She stands on the far shore of the ocean whose opposite shore is far away, O Rāghava; there is no sea-road to her, and she is inaccessible from every direction."

sanskrit: śailāgre racitā durgā sā pūr devapuropamā vājivāraṇasaṃpūrṇā laṅkā paramadurjayā
english: "That fortress-city is built on the summit of a mountain, comparable to the city of the gods, filled with horses and elephants; Laṅkā is supremely difficult to conquer."

sanskrit: parighāś ca śataghnyaś ca yantrāṇi vividhāni ca śobhayanti purīṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇasya durātmanaḥ
english: "Iron crossbars, śataghnis, and various war-engines adorn the city of Laṅkā belonging to Rāvaṇa, that evil-souled one."

sanskrit: ayutaṃ rakṣasām atra paścimadvāram āśritam śūlahastā durādharṣāḥ sarve khaḍgāgrayodhinaḥ
english: "At the western gate ten thousand rākṣasas are stationed — all of them wielding spears and hard to assail, foremost swordsmen."

sanskrit: niyutaṃ rakṣasām atra dakṣiṇadvāram āśritam caturaṅgeṇa sainyena yodhās tatrāpy anuttamāḥ
english: "A hundred thousand rākṣasas are stationed at the southern gate — warriors with a four-fold army, and peerless combatants there as well."

sanskrit: prayutaṃ rakṣasām atra pūrvadvāraṃ samāśritam carmakhaḍgadharāḥ sarve tathā sarvāstrakovidāḥ
english: "A million rākṣasas are posted at the eastern gate — all bearing shields and swords, and all of them skilled in every weapon."

sanskrit: arbudaṃ rakṣasām atra uttaradvāram āśritam rathinaś cāśvavāhāś ca kulaputrāḥ supūjitāḥ
english: "Ten million rākṣasas are stationed at the northern gate — charioteers and cavalry, all of them nobly born and highly honored."

sanskrit: śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ madhyamaṃ gulmam āśritam yātudhānā durādharṣāḥ sāgrakoṭiś ca rakṣasām
english: "At the central garrison a hundred times a hundred thousand — that is, more than a crore — of yātudhānas, hard to assail, are posted."

sanskrit: te mayā saṃkramā bhagnāḥ parikhāś cāvapūritāḥ dagdhā ca nagarī laṅkā prākārāś cāvasāditāḥ
english: "Those drawbridges I have broken, the moats I have filled up, the city of Laṅkā I have burned, and the ramparts I have shattered."

sanskrit: yena kena tu mārgeṇa tarāma varuṇālayam hateti nagarī laṅkāṃ vānarair avadhāryatām
english: "Whatever route we take to cross the abode of Varuṇa, let it be settled among the monkeys that the city of Laṅkā is as good as slain."

sanskrit: aṅgado dvivido maindo jāmbavān panaso nalaḥ nīlaḥ senāpatiś caiva balaśeṣeṇa kiṃ tava
english: "Aṅgada, Dvivida, Mainda, Jāmbavān, Panasa, Nala, and Nīla the general — with these remaining forces, what more do you need?"

sanskrit: plavamānā hi gatvā tāṃ rāvaṇasya mahāpurīm saprakārāṃ sabhavanām ānayiṣyanti maithilīm
english: "Leaping across, they will go to that great city of Rāvaṇa — ramparts, mansions and all — and bring back the Maithilī."

sanskrit: evam ājñāpaya kṣipraṃ balānāṃ sarvasaṃgraham muhūrtena tu yuktena prasthānam abhirocaya
english: "Therefore, command quickly the full muster of the army and, choosing an auspicious hour, authorize the departure."
